text:
jamie: Quick heads-up — I ran a simulation and found a corner where proxy eviction smoothing lets a non-resident region accept a write during the grace window. Not a full blowup but risky for residency guarantees.

sana: Can you sketch the sequence? is this the case where the lease flips but proxy still has the old hint?

jamie: Exactly. Sequence is: resident A loses primary, control-plane flips to B, proxy smoothing delays eviction for ~30s, client retried -> routed to A's proxy which still forwards to local pool that thinks it's owner. Write lands in non-consented region.

leo: Ugh. So smoothing trades correctness for availability. We knew that but thought legal flags would gate it. Is the consent check happening early?

jamie: Consent check is downstream in the write path (after routing). Proxy routing only looks at residency hints for stickiness. We do a final consent/assertion at the KV owner, but by then the write has been applied locally and needs cross-region sweep.

maria: That cross-region sweep is the painful bit if PII/regulatory. Could we short-circuit: if a tenant has residency constraints, disallow smoothing for them?

sana: That's one option. Per-tenant smoothing blacklist. Simpler: make the proxy consult a quick authoritative flag from control-plane before accepting writes during a grace window. Cheap read.

leo: Control-plane read on every request adds latency and scale concerns. We already fan out too much on cold paths. Maybe only during a transition window we escalate to control-plane. Normal ops skip it.

dmitri: Another approach: change ordering — validate residency at proxy, reject immediately (return 409) instead of accepting and sweeping. App can retry to resident region. That keeps residency clean but increases visible errors.

maria: Legal folks prefer hard rejects over silent cross-region writes. So 409s are acceptable if documented and observable.

jamie: Agreed. We could make the proxy behavior tiered: for tenants with residency constraints -> strict mode (reject on ambiguity). For others -> soft smoothing.

sana: We also need telemetry hooks for this: count of rejected writes due to residency, and count of accepted-but-swept writes. Right now sweeping is buried in background jobs.

ops-bot: deploy-bot: canary deployed proxy v2 to staging at 1769200060 :white_check_mark:

leo: For implementation: minimal config change + control-plane toggle per-tenant. Pseudo-config:

```
proxy:
  eviction_grace: 30s
  residency_strict_for: [tenantA, tenantB]
```

We can plumb a fast control-plane endpoint /v1/tenant/residency?ts=...

dmitri: Consider corner where control-plane itself is partitioned. If we rely on it, we need fail-open vs fail-closed policy. Fail-open -> risk residency. Fail-closed -> risk availability.

maria: Legal says fail-open unacceptable for EU-regulated customers. So per-tenant fail-mode metadata is required.

jamie: Action items: 1) draft short RFC for proxy strict mode + control-plane fast check (owner: jamie) 2) add telemetry counters for residency-rejections/sweeps (owner: sana) 3) add per-tenant fail-mode metadata to tenancy API (owner: dmitri) 4) quick staging test simulating control-plane partition (owner: leo).

sana: I'll add dashboards for the counters and a synthetic job to hit the transition path.

leo: I'd like to propose an extra safety net: when a write is accepted in a non-resident region and a sweep is scheduled, tag the KV entry with an immutable "suspect_region" marker and surface it to the audit log. Makes post-hoc detection easier.

maria: Good call. audit + legal export hooks will make compliance reviews faster.

jamie: I'll start the RFC draft tonight. @maria can you loop in compliance on the proposed strict-mode semantics?

maria: Yep — pinging them now (cc: compliance) :eyes:

dmitri: One more thought — try to avoid extra control-plane reads by caching per-tenant residency strict flag in proxies with short TTL and aggressive invalidation on transitions. Reduces load and keeps correctness bounded.

jamie: Nice. Add that to RFC.

sana: Cool. If no objections, I'll create the telemetry tickets and a staging runbook for the canary.

leo: No objections. Thanks all.

jamie: Thanks — filing RFC link when it's up.
